claims.text: Applying a chromium carbide coating to boride-based components can improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
The intervention produces a chromium carbide layer on the boride-based component.
The chromium carbide layer acts as a barrier between the boride-based component and molten aluminum.
Preventing direct contact with molten aluminum reduces corrosion of the boride-based component.
The chromium carbide coating should remain effective during molten-aluminum exposure at 600–700 °C.
Coated components are predicted to have a 30% longer lifespan than uncoated boride-based components.
Uncoated boride-based components are the baseline for comparison.
Component lifespan is to be measured in hours of molten-aluminum exposure.
Coating thickness may influence the effectiveness of the chromium carbide coating.
Surface roughness may influence the effectiveness of the chromium carbide coating.
The composition of the aluminum alloy may influence the effectiveness of the chromium carbide coating.
The hypothesis is falsified if the coated components have a corrosion rate greater than or equal to that of uncoated controls.
The hypothesis is falsified if coating does not increase component lifespan by at least 20% relative to uncoated controls.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a 30% lifespan increase, but the falsification rule accepts any increase of at least 20%; therefore, a 20–29% increase would contradict the quantitative prediction without falsifying the stated hypothesis.
